record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
record.original_question: With the same cut-and-project setup and notation as in Problem 2.4.1, is there a choice of α and β for which the supremum over all aligned rectangles Ω of the number of distinct frequencies #ξ_(α,β)(Ω) is infinite?

evidence.quote: The following is a seemingly easier version of the previous problem. Problem 2.4.2 Is there a choice of α and β as above such that sup_{Ω∈R} #ξ(α,β)(Ω) = +∞, where R denotes the collection of aligned rectangles?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ be irrational. Consider the canonical codimension-$2$ cut-and-project scheme in which $\mathbb{R}^{4}=E^{\parallel}\oplus E^{\perp}$ is decomposed so that the "physical" $2$-plane $E^{\parallel}\simeq\mathbb{R}^{2}$ is the graph
$$E^{\parallel}=\{(s,t,\alpha s,\beta t):s,t\in\mathbb{R}\},$$
and $E^{\perp}\simeq\mathbb{R}^{2}$ is its orthogonal complement; let $\pi^{\parallel}:\mathbb{R}^{4}\to E^{\parallel}$ and $\pi^{\perp}:\mathbb{R}^{4}\to E^{\perp}$ be the natural projections. Fix a bounded window $W\subset E^{\perp}$ with non-empty interior whose boundary has measure zero (for instance, a fixed unit square aligned with the coordinate axes of $E^{\perp}$). Define the cut-and-project point set
$$\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}=\bigl\{\pi^{\parallel}(\mathbf{v}):\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{Z}^{4},\;\pi^{\perp}(\mathbf{v})\in W\bigr\}\subset E^{\parallel}\simeq\mathbb{R}^{2}.$$

For a bounded set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}$ and a point $x\in\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}$, the $\Omega$-patch at $x$ is the finite set
$$P_{\Omega}(x)=\bigl(\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}-x\bigr)\cap\Omega.$$
Two $\Omega$-patches $P_{\Omega}(x)$ and $P_{\Omega}(y)$ are declared equivalent if they are equal as subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{2}$. Each equivalence class $[P]$ has a well-defined asymptotic frequency
$$\mathrm{freq}([P])=\lim_{R\to\infty}\frac{\#\{x\in\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}\cap B_{R}(0):P_{\Omega}(x)=P\}}{\mathrm{vol}(B_{R}(0))},$$
which exists for almost every choice of $\alpha,\beta$. Let
$$\xi_{\alpha,\beta}(\Omega)=\{\mathrm{freq}([P]):P\text{ an equivalence class of }\Omega\text{-patches in }\Lambda_{\alpha,\beta}\}\subset\mathbb{R}_{>0}$$
and let $\#\xi_{\alpha,\beta}(\Omega)$ denote its cardinality. Let
$$\mathcal{R}=\{\,[a_{1},b_{1}]\times[a_{2},b_{2}]:a_{i}<b_{i}\,\}$$
be the collection of all axis-aligned rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$.

Question: Does there exist an irrational pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ such that
$$\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal{R}}\#\xi_{\alpha,\beta}(\Omega)=+\infty\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the "easier" variant of an open problem on patch-frequency cardinality for two-dimensional cut-and-project sets with aligned rectangular windows. Subsequent work by Haynes, Koivusalo, Julien, Walton and Sadun on gaps problems and statistics of patterns in typical cut-and-project sets gives bounds on the number of distinct patch frequencies (typically polylogarithmic in the patch size) but does not appear to settle whether, for some specific choice of $(\alpha,\beta)$, the supremum over aligned rectangular regions can be infinite. No source found explicitly resolves this particular question, so its status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Gaps problems and frequencies of patches in cut and project sets
status_evidence.snippet: bounds for the number of distinct frequencies of patches of size r ... almost always less than a power of log r
status_evidence.claim: Generic upper bounds on the number of distinct patch frequencies are known, but no explicit construction giving an infinite supremum over aligned rectangles is reported.

status_evidence.title: Statistics of patterns in typical cut and project sets (arXiv:1702.04041)
status_evidence.snippet: estimates for the rate of convergence of appearances of patches to their asymptotic frequencies
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies typical-case statistics of patches but does not address whether for some special $(\alpha,\beta)$ the rectangle-indexed frequency count can be unbounded.
